authors: Jintao Zhang, Kai Jiang, Jintao Chen, Xu Wang, Deyuan Liu, Jungang Li, Dechuang Chen, Ming Lin, Jingjiang Zhou, Haopeng Jin, Qi Jia, Xiaohang Wang, Yaole Wang, Zhanqiang Zhang, Ran Li, Zhengkun Huang, Shuyue Xiong, Yuji Wang, Zikun Dai, Hui He, Yang Luo, Mang Ning, Weiqi Feng, Chengyang Ye, Xinyue Lin, Min Zhao, Hongzhou Zhu, Hengkai Tan, Zeyuan Wang, Chendong Xiang, Kaiwen Zheng, Zhijie Deng, Fan Bao, Jianfei Chen, Jun Zhu

provenance.yearPolicy: Year of the cited arXiv edition
provenance.note: Diffusion classification follows Section 2.2: the DiT denoises dense audiovisual latents; block recurrence does not introduce an independent visual-token AR backbone. Scope includes both avatar generation and general video editing/spatial video; do not present every component as a talking-head method. Metadata agrees with the local collection; first submitted 2026-09-10. No public model-code availability claim is made.

title: FlowAct-R2: Beyond Talking Avatar via Streaming Multimodal References and Proactive Agent Planning
summary: FlowAct-R2 adapts the Seedance 2.0 Mini diffusion backbone to rolling prompts, audio, and changing multimodal references, with temporal reference alignment and noised history conditioning. A separate interaction agent plans and schedules behaviors that the generator realizes as a continuous video stream.
authors: Ziyao Huang, Zhengkun Rong, Shiyang Qin, Shuang Liang, Wentao Hu, Yuxuan Luo, Yuan Zhang, Mingyuan Gao

provenance.yearPolicy: Year of the cited arXiv edition
provenance.note: Sections 2.1–2.2 assign dense video synthesis to the reference-to-video DiT and behavior planning to a separate agent; classify the visual generator as diffusion. The arXiv first-submission date is 2026-09-28; the manuscript title block says September 29, 2026. Use the arXiv date for chronological filtering. The paper links a Hugging Face demo Space; this does not establish a public model-code release.

title: PixReenact: Pixel-Conditioned Causal Video Diffusion for Streaming Head-Avatar Reenactment
summary: PixReenact conditions a causal video diffusion model directly on encoded reference and driving-video pixels for cross-identity head reenactment. Dual-teacher distillation trains a four-step rolling denoiser that emits four frames per update, using one latent of driving-video lookahead.
authors: Gavriel Habib, Dvir Samuel, Or Shimshi, Rami Ben-Ari

provenance.yearPolicy: Year of the cited arXiv edition
provenance.note: Sections 3.2–3.4 and Appendix A identify a Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B DiT adapted with causal attention, LoRA, and CausVid-style DMD; dense visual latents remain diffusion-generated. Driving conditioning includes one-latent lookahead. The authors say this fits inside their rolling pipeline without additional emission delay; it is not zero-lookahead input causality. The official project URL is linked in the paper but returned a fetch error during verification. Public code was not verified.

title: Where and When to Force: Routed Forcing for Streaming Avatars
summary: Routed Forcing applies real-data distillation supervision to non-mouth person regions at high noise while retaining distribution matching elsewhere. This trains a causal OmniAvatar diffusion student to preserve motion diversity, lip synchronization, and scene quality during streaming.
authors: Zihan Su, Siwen Lu, Junhao Zhuang, Zeyue Xue, Haoyang Huang, Guanghao Li, Xiaofeng Tan, Chun Yuan, Nan Duan

provenance.yearPolicy: Year of the cited arXiv edition
provenance.note: Section 4.1 uses a causal OmniAvatar-1.3B student initialized from LiveTalk and a bidirectional OmniAvatar-14B teacher; inference uses three latent frames per block and four denoising steps. The innovation changes diffusion-training supervision rather than visual-state ownership. Generalization beyond streaming avatars is left open in Section 4.4. Metadata agrees with the local collection. No official project or public code link was verified in the original paper.

title: DynaForcing: Overcoming Dynamic Collapse in Self-Forcing Distillation for Streaming Avatar Generation
summary: DynaForcing addresses motion collapse during self-forcing distillation through data-anchored rollout starts, dynamics rewards, and reference-image perturbations. Its WanS2V diffusion student retains chunked streaming inference, while gradient replay reduces training memory requirements.
authors: Yubo Huang, Sirui Zhao, Xinchen Yao, Zhengye Zhang, Jinyang Huang, Fengqi Cui, Shiwei Wu, Enhong Chen

provenance.yearPolicy: Year of the cited arXiv edition
provenance.note: The arXiv comments report acceptance at ACM International Conference on Multimedia (MM 2026); no proceedings DOI or page range was verified. The BibTeX below cites the arXiv version and records that reported acceptance. Sections 3–5 retain WanS2V-14B dense-video diffusion with LiveAvatar diffusion-forcing pretraining; the contribution changes training rather than replacing the visual generator. Reported throughput uses a single H800 node at 720×400; do not restate this as a verified single-GPU result. Public code was not verified.

title: Avatar-Forever: Decoupled Parallel Training for High-Quality Real-Time Infinite Avatars
summary: Avatar-Forever independently trains a four-step distilled video generator and a recovery adapter that learns from accumulated rollout errors, then combines them for audio-driven avatars. ForeverCache reuses history features across denoising steps to accelerate streaming generation.
authors: Ruibin Li, Tao Yang, Zhiyuan Ma, Fangzhou Ai, Shilei Wen, Lei Zhang

provenance.yearPolicy: Year of the cited arXiv edition
provenance.note: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain an LTX dense-video denoiser; DMD and flow-matching recovery training place visual generation in the diffusion route. Author discrepancy: arXiv lists six authors including Shilei Wen; the project page and repository citation list five and omit him. The metadata and BibTeX here follow arXiv. The official repository contains inference code and a model download link. Its documented checkpoint uses LTX 2.3 22B; project examples beyond avatars should not be treated as an avatar-specific benchmark.

title: Wan-Animate-2: Pushing the Application Boundaries of Character Animation
summary: Wan-Animate-2-Lite converts the paper’s character-animation diffusion model into a causal generator that processes eight-frame driving-video chunks. Teacher forcing, error-buffer conditioning, and self-forcing distillation address accumulated context errors and denoising cost.
authors: Guangyuan Wang, Li Hu, Dechao Meng, Zhongyi Zhang, Peng Zhang, Xindi Zhang, Mingyang Huang, Ruoshi Zhang, Ke Sun, Zhe Zhang, Xingjun Wang, Gang Cheng, Hai Xu, Bang Zhang

provenance.yearPolicy: Year of the cited arXiv edition
provenance.note: One paper entry covers Base and Lite; the streaming description is specifically Lite (Section 4, Figure 2). Base uses a dual-branch DiT and is not established as the same streaming system. First submitted 2026-08-06; current v2 dated 2026-08-08 was verified. The local collection links v1. Repository release notes name Base and Distillation models, not a verified Lite checkpoint. Its BibTeX has a placeholder arXiv ID, a different title, and omits Xindi Zhang and Hai Xu; use the arXiv metadata below.

title: Vorch-Streamer: Extending Human Audio-Visual Generation to Real-Time Long-Form Streaming
summary: Vorch-Streamer adapts LTX2.3 to jointly generate audio and video through block-causal flow matching and four-step self-forcing distillation. A speech-planning language model conditions the audio branch, while bounded visual history supports long-form avatar streaming.
authors: Menglin Han, Yang Ding, Yulei Lu, Haoran Yu, Xin Ma, Junyi Chen, Zhangkai Ni, Lin Ma, Yaohui Wang

provenance.yearPolicy: Year of the cited arXiv edition
provenance.note: Sections 3.2–3.4 preserve bidirectional attention within approximately one-second blocks and causal bounded history across blocks. The external language model plans speech; the LTX diffusion backbone owns dense visual generation. First submitted 2026-08-06; current v2 dated 2026-08-07 was verified. The local collection links v1. The official project code link remains marked Coming soon. Evaluation targets joint text-to-audio-video generation, so audio-conditioned avatar baselines have different inputs.
